incidents.vector: FBI warned that the Silent Ransom Group impersonates internal IT staff via phone and phishing email to gain remote access, and when that fails sends an operative to the victim's office to physically plug a storage device into a workstation and copy files.
incidents.impact: The Russia-based group, active since 2022 with more than 100 claimed attacks, has surged activity in recent months against law firms — exfiltrating client data to leak sites and demanding ransoms to suppress publication; the legal sector was the fourth most-targeted industry by ransomware actors in Q1 2026.

incidents.vector: Paris prosecutors opened a foreign-interference probe into deceptive websites, fake social media accounts and digital ads accusing three hard-left mayoral candidates of criminal behaviour, coordinated by an opaque influence-for-hire firm called BlackCore.
incidents.impact: The probe — folding in earlier investigations in Marseille and Toulouse and adding a specialized national cyber police unit — covers suspected foreign espionage, election fraud via false information, and online advocacy of terrorism; BlackCore scrubbed its online presence after Reuters enquiries.

incidents.vector: A 35-year-old man arrested in Buren is suspected of repeatedly exploiting an unpatched vulnerability in Ajax's web systems to enter the club's computers.
incidents.impact: Ajax originally said only emails of a few hundred individuals and details of a small number of banned supporters were exposed, but Dutch broadcaster RTL reported the breach may have touched personal data of more than 300,000 supporters and over 42,000 season tickets, and could have allowed ticket transfers and edits to stadium-ban records.

incidents.vector: Russia-based operators ran a botnet using Solana blockchain, BitTorrent, Google Calendar and rented VPS infrastructure to push malware into VS Code extensions, npm and Python packages and more than 300 GitHub repositories since early 2025.
incidents.impact: CrowdStrike, Google, and Shadowserver simultaneously seized four attacker servers, disrupting the botnet's command channels and the GlasswormRAT remote-access tool that had stolen data and credentials from Windows, macOS and Linux developer machines worldwide.

incidents.vector: Dutch financial-crime investigators (FIOD) arrested the 39-year-old MIRhosting owner and a 57-year-old Amsterdam associate on May 18 for violating EU sanctions by providing connectivity to entities that hosted Russia-linked cyber and influence operations.
incidents.impact: FIOD raided three businesses and two data centres in Enschede, Almere, Dronten and Schiphol-Rijk, seizing laptops, phones and more than 800 servers; customer data on those servers was lost. The seizure cuts off the last major Stark Industries upstream provider after May 2025 EU sanctions against PQHosting.

incidents.victim: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA)
incidents.vector: Iranian operators posing as a hacktivist crew named 'Ababil of Minab' breached LACMTA in mid-March, then used scripts and hands-on-keyboard actions to wipe databases, virtual machines, backups and storage volumes.
incidents.impact: At least 700 GB of email, backups and other files were exfiltrated and parts of the transit network were forced offline; Israeli researchers at Gambit Security tied the group to Iran's intelligence service after data was inadvertently exposed online, adding forensic backing to the long-suspected state link.

incidents.victim: Tri-Rail (South Florida commuter rail) and Vyncs (vehicle tracking)
incidents.vector: The Iran-linked 'Ababil of Minab' persona — the same group behind the LACMTA wiper attack — also claimed responsibility for breaches at Tri-Rail and at vehicle tracking company Vyncs, which detected its intrusion on April 2.
incidents.impact: Tri-Rail confirmed a hack but said no critical data was affected; Vyncs owner Agnik declined to characterize the stolen data and is working with the FBI. The cluster of US transportation-sector hits underscores expanded Iranian targeting of transit and mobility infrastructure.

incidents.victim: Unimac (Saudi infrastructure firm) and other regional targets
incidents.vector: Same Iran-MOIS persona ('Ababil of Minab') breached Saudi infrastructure company Unimac and additional unnamed targets including an Israeli media organization, an Israeli university and a Turkish insurance brokerage.
incidents.impact: Data was exfiltrated from each target; Unimac did not respond to requests for comment, and the broader campaign demonstrates Iran's continued use of fake-hacktivist personas to target regional adversaries and critical infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Attackers believed to be affiliated with the Chinese government used phishing to access Microsoft 365 mailboxes of Wiley Rein staff between July 2024 and June 2025, before the firm detected the intrusion last year; the suit alleges MFA and basic safeguards were absent.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses, dates of birth, financial account numbers, medical information and Social Security numbers were stolen; the firm only began notifying victims on or around March 6, 2026, and is now facing a proposed class action in DC federal court (Burkett v. Wiley Rein).

incidents.vector: A six-hour automated campaign codenamed 'Megalodon' used dummy accounts and forged author identities to push 5,718 malicious commits into 5,561 GitHub repositories on May 18, injecting GitHub Actions workflows that exfiltrate CI/CD secrets, cloud credentials, SSH keys, OpenID Connect tokens and source code secrets.
incidents.impact: A second-stage payload replaces existing workflows with a dormant 'workflow-dispatch' backdoor that produces no visible CI runs; researchers say roughly 83% of affected repos remained infected more than a week later, and downstream npm package @tiledesk/tiledesk-server was poisoned and republished to users.

incidents.vector: Operators ran SEO poisoning that placed lookalike download sites for CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, FurMark, K-Lite Codec Pack and other utilities in search results and — newly — in AI chatbot responses; victims downloaded ZIPs from gleeze.com subdomains that delivered crypto-mining payloads alongside ScreenConnect remote-access agents.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Defender Experts blocked the campaign but warns the persistent ScreenConnect footprint could later be repurposed for data theft, lateral movement or ransomware; the campaign deliberately targets high-end GPU systems to maximize mining yield per host.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations in US, UK, Australia (M365/Okta tenants)
incidents.vector: Threat actor UNC6671 ('BlackFile') runs high-volume voice phishing against employees' personal phones, posing as IT for a passkey/MFA migration and steering them to lookalike SSO portals on enrollms[.]com, passkeyms[.]com and setupsso[.]com to harvest credentials and MFA codes in real time.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence Group says dozens of organizations have been compromised and had M365, SharePoint, OneDrive, Zendesk and Salesforce data exfiltrated for extortion; UNC6671 has at times misused the ShinyHunters brand to add credibility to extortion threats.

incidents.victim: Aerospace, defense and telecom firms in US, Israel, UAE
incidents.vector: Iran-nexus APT 'Screening Serpens' (UNC1549) used spear-phishing job-recruitment lures and DLL sideloading; a new AppDomainManager hijacking technique disables .NET application security mechanisms to deploy six new RAT variants in two families (MiniUpdate and MiniJunk V2).
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed espionage operations against US, Israeli and UAE entities plus two additional Middle Eastern organizations between mid-February and April 2026, aligned with the regional conflict that began Feb. 28, 2026; the actor maintains 3-5 unique Azure-hosted C2 domains per target to prevent cross-contamination.

incidents.vector: A Nightwing contractor administering CISA's code platform created a public GitHub repo called 'Private-CISA' in November 2025 and intentionally disabled GitHub's built-in secret-scanning protection, exposing AWS GovCloud admin keys, plaintext passwords for dozens of internal CISA systems, and an RSA private key for a CISA-IT GitHub app.
incidents.impact: More than a week after notification CISA was still rotating leaked credentials; Senator Maggie Hassan and Reps. Bennie Thompson and Delia Ramirez demanded answers, warning the exposure handed China, Russia and Iran a roadmap into federal networks during a period of major CISA workforce cuts.

incidents.victim: Kimwolf DDoS botnet (millions of IoT devices)
incidents.vector: A 23-year-old Ottawa resident allegedly built and rented out an IoT botnet that enslaved millions of cameras, photo frames and similar devices, generating record DDoS attacks measured near 30 Tbps including hits against US Department of Defense IP ranges.
incidents.impact: Canadian police arrested the suspect on a US extradition warrant; some victims incurred losses exceeding $1 million and the botnet issued over 25,000 attack commands before international takedowns of Kimwolf, Aisuru, JackSkid and Mossad infrastructure.

incidents.vector: TeamPCP (TGR-CRI-1135) ran two more waves of the 'Mini Shai-Hulud' worm in May, including one using a credential-free initial-access technique that produced npm packages with valid SLSA provenance, and another that set the highest single-hour malicious-package count of any Shai-Hulud wave.
incidents.impact: The wormable payloads steal npm tokens and GitHub PATs, republish themselves into legitimate packages, and embed into CI/CD pipelines for long-term access; the @bitwarden/cli v2026.4.0 trojan and Docker Hub, GitHub Actions and VS Code extension variants stole cloud, CI/CD and workstation credentials from developers globally.

incidents.victim: US private health insurers ($2B fraud loss)
incidents.vector: A Moscow-based criminal organization ran call centers in Utah and later Russia that contacted insured patients with offers of free medications, generated fraudulent prescriptions via ghost telemedicine visits, and used straw-owned US pharmacies plus Moscow-based remote billers to submit reimbursement requests under stolen physician identifiers.
incidents.impact: Between 2017 and 2022 the ring submitted more than $1.97 billion in fraudulent prescriptions through over 75 pharmacies in Brooklyn, Staten Island, Long Island and New Jersey; ringleader Brian Sutton remains at large abroad while three co-defendants were sentenced this month to 10, 10 and 8 years.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — sophisticated actor (UAT-8616) plus multiple clusters
incidents.vector: Talos confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-20182, an authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager that grants admin access without credentials; separately, multiple actors are chaining CVE-2026-20133, -20128 and -20122 using ZeroZenX Labs' public PoC and a JSP webshell dubbed 'XenShell' to drop webshells and tooling on unpatched SD-WAN Manager systems.
incidents.impact: UAT-8616 — a sophisticated actor whose infrastructure overlaps known Operational Relay Box networks — added SSH keys, modified NETCONF configs and escalated to root on victim networks; Talos has identified at least ten post-compromise activity clusters since March 2026.

incidents.vector: HealthSplash CEO Brett Blackman and co-conspirators used the company's DMERx internet-based platform to generate fake doctors' orders and prescriptions for durable medical equipment, paid kickbacks to telemedicine companies that signed orders without seeing patients, and used foreign call centers and spam mailers to recruit elderly beneficiaries.
incidents.impact: A federal jury in the Southern District of Florida convicted Blackman on May 14, finding the platform billed Medicare and other federal programs more than $1 billion for medically unnecessary orthotic braces and similar items targeting hundreds of thousands of seniors, veterans and service members.
